text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- The draft law on protective tariffs, which reached its first reading yesterday, imposes tariffs on a large number of articles like tropical fruit and vegetables, exotic animals, and heavy military hardware. Opposition members call the law absurd and harmful to Estonia's reputation.
- The refresher course for reserve officers continues in Vodru; the group contains a number of high-ranking government officials and well-known public figures.
- The Tallinn city council failed to vote deputy mayor Kalev Kallo out of office.
- Police have arrested a serial killer, who is suspected of killing three elderly women last autumn.
- The Tallinn heating company wants to lower the rates for industry and raise those for the individual users in order to end subsidies to the population.
